chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

The marriage of temporary enjoyment (Mut'ah) is a marriage with inheritance and a marriage without inheritance. If inheritance is stipulated, it is [with inheritance], and if it is not stipulated, it is not [with inheritance].
ai.seo_question: Does temporary marriage (Mut'ah) include inheritance rights in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that temporary marriage (Nikah al-Mut'ah) is a valid contract where inheritance rights are not automatic but contingent upon explicit stipulation (ishtirat) within the agreement. This ruling highlights the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing Mut'ah from permanent marriage where inheritance is inherent, thereby allowing parties to tailor the legal consequences of their union. This principle underscores the contractual nature of Mut'ah, emphasizing that the absence of an inheritance clause does not invalidate the marriage itself.
